w:r.w:t: Finance & Expense Management Module - Complete Documentation
(Multi-Tier Approval by Amount - Email & Dashboard Notifications - Budget-Controlled)

The Finance Module serves as the central hub for all monetary transactions within the ERP system. All money flows through Finance - both income coming IN and expenses going OUT. The key feature of this module is that ALL expenses, regardless of amount or category, require CEO approval. All approval requests are delivered exclusively through dashboard notifications - Email + Dashboard are sent.

2.1 Role Summary - Segregation of Duties Applied
Record all sales revenue from all modules
Track customer credit balances, record payments
Track aging of receivables and payables

The Finance Officer receives cash from Sales Manager for retail sales, pays suppliers after Purchase Officer creates POs, pays salaries after HR Manager calculates payroll, and reports to CEO. All expense payments require tiered approval (Manager/Director/CEO based on amount). A separate Payment Processor role executes approved payments. Finance Officer records the expense but does NOT have payment execution rights. An Accountant performs reconciliation and is independent of both recording and payment.

Cashier collects cash from customers and gives to Sales Manager. Sales Manager verifies and consolidates cash from all cashiers and hands over to Finance Officer. Finance Officer records the income and deposits to bank.
Purchase Officer creates POs and sends to suppliers. When supplier invoice arrives, Finance Officer records expense and submits to CEO for approval. After CEO approval, Finance Officer pays supplier.

HR Manager calculates monthly payroll and submits to Finance Officer. Finance Officer records salary expense and submits to CEO for approval. After CEO approval, Finance Officer processes salary payments.
CEO approves ALL expenses via dashboard notifications. CEO reviews financial reports and provides strategic oversight.

FIN-001: Record Income from Sales Channels
The system shall automatically record income from all sales channels including Retail Store, Pharmacy, Farming, Printing, Car Rental, and Tender/Bid. Income recording does not require CEO approval.

The Finance Officer shall be able to manually enter operational expenses with categories including Salary, Rent, Utilities, Supplies, Maintenance, Supplier Payment, Tax, and Other. All expenses require CEO approval before payment can be processed.

The Finance Officer shall process supplier payments against approved POs. The expense must first be approved by CEO via dashboard notification. After approval, Finance Officer can process the payment.
The Finance Officer shall record bank deposits for cash received from sales. This does not require CEO approval.
The system shall track customer credit balances when customers select "Credit" as payment method at POS. This does not require CEO approval.
The system shall track supplier balances for unpaid POs. This does not require CEO approval.
FIN-007: ALL Expenses Require CEO Approval

The system shall require CEO approval for ALL expenses regardless of amount or category. There is NO auto-approval for any expense. Every single expense entry must be approved by CEO before payment can be processed.
The system shall send notifications to CEO dashboard for ALL expense approval requests. Email + Dashboard shall be sent. CEO sees pending approvals immediately upon login to the dashboard.
The system shall generate a Daily Sales Report showing income from all sources.
The system shall generate a Weekly Profit & Loss Statement showing revenue, COGS, expenses, and net profit.
The system shall generate a Monthly Balance Sheet showing assets, liabilities, and equity.
The system shall generate a Cash Flow Statement showing operating, investing, and financing activities.
The system shall generate an Accounts Receivable Aging Report showing customer balances by aging buckets: Current (0-30 days), Past Due (31-60 days), Delinquent (61-90 days), and Critical (90+ days).
The system shall generate an Accounts Payable Aging Report showing supplier balances by aging buckets: Current (0-30 days), Past Due (31-60 days), Delinquent (61-90 days), and Critical (90+ days).
The Finance Officer shall manually verify and record payments received via Bank Transfer and Telebirr. Customer uploads proof of payment and Finance Officer verifies and updates payment status.
The Finance Officer shall process customer refunds. All refunds require CEO approval before processing.
The Finance Officer shall record tax payments made to government. All tax payments require CEO approval.
The Finance Officer shall perform monthly bank reconciliation to match system records with bank statements.
The system shall allow exporting reports to PDF and Excel formats.

5.1 Expense Categories - Multi-Tier Approval by Amount
The Finance Officer records an expense by filling out the following form:
Category: Dropdown selection (Salary, Rent, Utilities, Supplies, Maintenance, Supplier Payment, Tax, Other)
Description: Enter detailed description of expense
Department: Dropdown selection (Printing, Pharmacy, Car Rental, Farming, Retail, Admin)
Receipt Attachment: Upload file (PDF, PNG, JPEG - Max 5MB)

For expenses under 1,000 ETB, the Finance Officer may use the Petty Cash fund instead of the approval workflow. Petty Cash expenses are tracked separately and reconciled monthly by the Accountant. For standard expenses, after filling out the form, the Finance Officer clicks "SUBMIT FOR APPROVAL". The system checks the department budget. If sufficient budget exists, the system creates the expense record with status PENDING_APPROVAL and routes it to the appropriate approver (Manager/Director/CEO) based on the amount. The approver receives an email notification with a direct link, and a dashboard notification appears in the notification center.

8.5 Ethiopian Tax Compliance (ERCA/MoF) 8.5.1 Value Added Tax (VAT): VAT rate: 15% on taxable goods and services. VAT Registration threshold: annual turnover exceeding 1,000,000 ETB. VAT on Sales (Output VAT): automatically calculated on all sales transactions. VAT on Purchases (Input VAT): captured from supplier invoices. VAT Return: Monthly filing to ERCA/MoF by the 15th of the following month. VAT Report includes: Output VAT summary by rate, Input VAT summary, Net VAT payable/refundable. 8.5.2 Withholding Tax: Purchases from non-registered suppliers: 2% withholding. Purchases from registered suppliers: 50% of VAT withholding. Service withholding: 15% for certain professional services. Rental income withholding: 15%. Withholding Tax Return: Monthly filing with VAT return. 8.5.3 Employment Income Tax: Monthly PAYE calculation based on Ethiopian tax brackets. Monthly remittance to ERCA by the 7th of the following month. Annual income tax reconciliation for each employee. 8.5.4 Pension Contributions: Employee contribution: 7% of gross salary. Employer contribution: 11% of gross salary. Monthly remittance to Public Service Pension Agency / Private Organization. 8.5.5 Tax Reports: VAT 7.1 Monthly Report, Withholding Tax Monthly Report, Income Tax Annual Report, Pension Contribution Report. All tax reports printable and exportable to ERCA/MoF format. 8.5.6 Tax Audit Trail: Complete history of all tax calculations, returns filed, and payments made. Tax payment approval: all tax payments require CEO approval (Tier 3). 8.6 Accounts Payable Aging

10.1 Chart of Accounts (COA) Structure The system shall maintain a hierarchical Chart of Accounts with the following structure: Account Type, Account Code, Account Name, Parent Account, Is Active, Normal Balance. Major account types: 1xxx - Assets (Current Assets: 11xx Cash, 12xx Accounts Receivable, 13xx Inventory; Fixed Assets: 14xx Equipment, 15xx Vehicles, 16xx Furniture; Accumulated Depreciation: 17xx). 2xxx - Liabilities (Current: 21xx Accounts Payable, 22xx Accrued Expenses; Long-Term: 23xx Bank Loans). 3xxx - Equity (31xx Owner Capital, 32xx Retained Earnings). 4xxx - Revenue (41xx Sales Revenue, 42xx Service Revenue, 43xx Other Income). 5xxx - Cost of Goods Sold (51xx COGS - Printing, 52xx COGS - Pharmacy, etc.). 6xxx - Operating Expenses (61xx Salaries, 62xx Rent, 63xx Utilities, 64xx Supplies, 65xx Maintenance, 66xx Depreciation, 67xx Tax Expense). Each transaction posts to at least two accounts (double-entry accounting). Account codes are 4 digits with hierarchical grouping. 10.2 Expense Table

12.6 Month-End Close Process 12.6.1 Close Schedule: Close occurs on the last business day of each month. No new transactions can be posted to the closed period. Only adjusting entries by the Accountant are allowed after close. 12.6.2 Close Checklist: Verify all bank transactions are reconciled. Post all depreciation entries. Post all accrued expenses (salaries, utilities, interest). Post prepaid expense amortization. Reconcile all inter-department transactions. Verify AR and AP aging reports. Run trial balance and verify it balances. Run financial reports (P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow). Review budget vs actual variances. File monthly tax returns (VAT, Withholding, PAYE, Pension). Lock period to prevent further changes. 12.6.3 Close Approval: Accountant runs close checklist. Finance Officer reviews and signs off. CEO provides final close approval. 12.6.4 Period Locking: Closed periods are locked and cannot be modified. Adjusting entries require Accountant role and create audit trail. Re-opening a period requires CEO approval. 12.7 Usability Requirements

ALL expenses follow this workflow regardless of amount or category:
Finance Officer records expense with category, amount, description, department, and attachment.
Finance Officer submits expense for approval. Status becomes PENDING_APPROVAL.
System adds notification to CEO Dashboard with expense details and APPROVE, REJECT, VIEW DETAILS buttons.
CEO logs in to dashboard and sees pending approvals count.
CEO clicks VIEW DETAILS to see full expense information including description, attachments, and justification.
CEO takes one of three actions:
a. APPROVE - Expense status becomes APPROVED. Finance Officer notified on dashboard.
b. REJECT - CEO provides reason. Expense status becomes REJECTED. Finance Officer notified on dashboard.
c. REQUEST MORE INFO - CEO asks question. Expense status becomes NEEDS_INFO. Finance Officer notified on dashboard. Finance Officer adds info and re-submits.
After CEO approval, Finance Officer processes payment. Expense status becomes PAID.
Email + Dashboard ARE SENT AT ANY STAGE. All notifications are on dashboard only.
